svg.title: Stable eigenvalues do not preclude transient amplification
svg.desc: The spectral norm of exp(t A K) is plotted for upper triangular stable matrices with couplings zero, five and twenty. Larger nonnormal coupling produces a higher finite-time peak although both eigenvalues remain negative.
svg.text: Stable eigenvalues can hide finite-time amplification
A_K = [[−1, K], [0, −2]] has α(A_K) = −1 for every K, but ||exp(tA_K)||₂ depends strongly on K
All curves decay to zero as t → ∞. The peak is a finite-time, direction-dependent effect caused by nonnormal coupling—not unstable eigenvalues.
